children: Used-car marketplace Spinny confidentially pre-files IPO papers for a Rs 2,500-3,000 crore issue, targeting a potential 2027 listing

Used-car marketplace Spinny has confidentially pre-filed its IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India for a proposed Rs 2,500-3,000 crore issue, comprising a combination of fresh shares and an offer for sale, as per a media report

The Gurugram-based startup is targeting a potential stock market listing in 2027, although the timeline will depend on regulatory approvals. The final issue size and structure could also change during the IPO process
Spinny has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India, Morgan Stanley India and 360 ONE WAM as book-running lead managers for the proposed issue
The confidential filing comes after Spinny's parent company, Valuedrive Technologies, converted from a private limited company into a public limited company in August

Spinny's operating revenue grew nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to around Rs 6,000 crore in FY26, with the company expecting another 25-30 per cent growth in the ongoing fiscal year, according to the report

In FY25, Spinny's operating revenue increased 25 per cent to Rs 4,656.1 crore from Rs 3,729.8 crore in FY24. Its net loss narrowed 28 per cent to Rs 423.8 crore from Rs 590.3 crore during the previous fiscal year
The company is yet to file its audited financial statements for FY26

In February 2026, Spinny raised USD 170 million in a funding round led by Fidelity Investments and Accel Leaders Fund. The round included USD 90 million in primary capital and USD 80 million through secondary share sales
The funding round valued Spinny at around USD 1.5 billion, lower than its USD 1.7 billion valuation in May 2025, when it raised USD 131 million to strengthen its non-banking financial company arm
Spinny has raised more than USD 784 million to date from investors including Accel, Tiger Global, General Catalyst, Fidelity, WestBridge Capital and Sachin Tendulkar
Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh, Mohit Gupta and Ramanshu Mahaur, Spinny operates a full-stack used-car retail platform. The company acquires, refurbishes, holds and resells vehicles
It also offers ancillary services including vehicle financing, insurance, warranties, servicing and maintenance
Spinny is among several used-car startups exploring public listings. Cars24 and CarDekho have also been considering IPO plans, while CarTrade Tech is already listed on Indian stock exchanges
